overall: Tomorrow (Tuesday, June 23) in Atlanta is expected to be partly sunny with a slight chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms (20% PoP), primarily between noon and 3pm. West winds of 5–10 mph with gusts to 20 mph suggest a post-frontal air mass moving in after tonight's more active storm activity. Conditions should be more benign than today, but lingering cloud cover from overnight storms could suppress afternoon heating.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is notably poor, with a very wide spread: HRRR is the coolest at ~78.1°F (consistent with the full ensemble's 79.2°F), GFS at ~81.8°F, ECMWF at ~83.2°F, WEATHER_COM at ~85.0°F, and NBM is the warmest outlier at ~87.2°F — nearly matching the NWS narrative of 86°F. The full ensemble model (which incorporates prior-day observations) skews significantly cooler than the NWS narrative and the NBM/WEATHER_COM suite, suggesting observation-based corrections are pulling the forecast down from the purely model-driven outputs.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble expected TMAX of 79.2°F, anchored by the top probability bucket of 78–79°F at 20.9%, represents the best single estimate; the forecast-only model's 81.7°F is a secondary reference. Key cooling factors include overnight storms (70% PoP tonight) that could limit boundary layer recovery, a west/northwest wind shift indicative of post-frontal air, and the prior-day observed high of only 80.6°F providing a realistic baseline. Confidence is low-to-moderate given wide inter-model spread (nearly 9°F between HRRR and NBM) and the Tier 4 (Poor) odd-bucket signal; the even-bucket Tier 2 signal offers modest confidence around the 78–83°F zone.
